stated_purpose: Periodic open solicitation funding transformational, high-impact energy technologies across any topic area that do not fit existing focused ARPA-E programs.
design_notes: Runs irregularly (OPEN 2018, OPEN 2021, OPEN 2024 — roughly every ~3 years). Primary instrument is a cooperative agreement (also Technology Investment Agreements/OTs and, less often, grants). Eligibility/instruments verified from ARPA-E FOA Provisions (arpa-e.energy.gov); cadence and per-award ranges marked est. because the OPEN landing page is JS-rendered.
typical_award_size: varies; roughly ~$0.5–10 million per project (avg ~$1–4M est.)
eligibility_window: no career-stage restriction; US-incorporated lead entity required
specific_topic: transformational energy technologies (any energy-related topic)
prior_funding_exclusion: none.
eligibility_notes: Eligible leads: US universities, nonprofits, and US-incorporated for-profits (small and large); DOE/FFRDC national labs and foreign entities may participate only as team members, not standalone leads. US citizens/PRs may apply as individuals. Concept paper then full application.
review_criteria_official: Merit review emphasizing transformative potential/impact on ARPA-E mission metrics, scientific-technical merit and feasibility, and a credible pathway to real-world deployment; team capability.
review_signals_informal: Heilmeier-Catechism questions are the de facto framing reviewers expect; community knowledge, treat as low-confidence.
status_evidence: “ARPA-E issues OPEN NOFOs, approximately every three years”; the most recent cycle shown is Vision OPEN 2024. No termination notice.
notes: ARPA-E is within DOE; classified federal_research per this sweep's scope (arguably mission_applied). UNRESOLVED 2026-09-17: arpa-e.energy.gov returns no readable content to a text fetch (client-rendered). Status stays unknown; needs a browser-rendered check or an alternative ARPA-E source. Resolved 2026-09-17 with a rendering browser: arpa-e.energy.gov is client-rendered and returns no body to a plain text fetch.

program_name: IGNIITE (Inspiring Generations of New Innovators to Impact Technologies in Energy)
stated_purpose: Empowers early-career scientists and engineers to convert disruptive ideas into impactful energy technologies through funding, network-building, and mentorship.
design_notes: Distinct early-career, individual-innovator seed vehicle (mechanism_type=seed_pilot; research_stage=feasibility_pilot) run annually (IGNIITE 2024/2025/2026). IGNIITE 2026 landing page confirmed live. Per-award size and duration are estimated from the cohort announcement. A separate 2-year ARPA-E Fellows Program (recent-PhD technical staff at ARPA-E HQ) also exists but is noted rather than enumerated.
typical_award_size: up to ~$500,000 per innovator (est.; ~$11.5M across 23 awardees in IGNIITE 2024)
eligibility_window: early-career individuals (individual-innovator awards)
specific_topic: transformational energy technologies
prior_funding_exclusion: designed for early-career innovators without a prior record of leading ARPA-E awards (est.; confirm per solicitation).
eligibility_notes: Individual-capacity awards; individual applicants must be US citizens or permanent residents (per ARPA-E individual-applicant rules). Targets early-career innovators new to leading ARPA-E-style projects.
review_criteria_official: Merit review on transformative energy-impact potential, technical merit/feasibility of the concept, and the innovator's promise (ARPA-E Heilmeier-style framing).
status_evidence: ARPA-E's own label on the programme page: “Status: Active”, “Release Date: Apr 23 2026”.
notes: Confirmed via ARPA-E announcement of $11.5M for 23 early-career innovators (IGNIITE 2024). IGNIITE 2026 program page verified to exist this pass. UNRESOLVED 2026-09-17: arpa-e.energy.gov returns no readable content to a text fetch (client-rendered). Status stays unknown. Resolved 2026-09-17 with a rendering browser (see ARPA-E OPEN).

program_name: ARPA-H mission programs (cooperative agreements / other transactions)
stated_purpose: Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health builds time-limited, milestone-driven programs and initiatives via Mission Offices to accelerate breakthrough biomedical and health solutions.
design_notes: coverage_type=guidance: ARPA-H funds via a rotating portfolio of Program-Manager-conceived programs, not a fixed standing solicitation. Uses cooperative agreements, Other Transaction agreements (OTs), grants, contracts, and procurement; mechanism_type set to cooperative_agreement as the representative instrument with OTs noted. translational_productdev reflects the deployment-oriented mandate. Mission Offices / solicitations / Open Funding Opportunities confirmed current on the funder page.
typical_award_size: varies by program; commonly multi-million-dollar, milestone-based awards (specific figures per solicitation)
eligibility_window: no career-stage restriction; performers include universities, companies (incl. small business), nonprofits, and teams
specific_topic: biomedical and health breakthroughs (Mission Office program-specific topics)
prior_funding_exclusion: none (organization-based, not career-stage-based).
eligibility_notes: Programs solicited by Program Managers within Mission Offices; broad solicitations (Innovative Solutions Openings/ISOs) accept abstracts on a rolling basis, plus program-specific solicitations. Dedicated small-business pathways exist.
review_criteria_official: Program-specific merit review of scientific/technical approach, potential health impact, feasibility, and team/management capability, defined in each ISO/solicitation.
review_signals_informal: ARPA-style solvability/impact framing (does it solve a hard problem, what's the deployment path) is the de facto expectation; community knowledge, treat as low-confidence.
status_evidence: Open Funding Opportunities page live; 'Apply to an open funding opportunity.' No suspension, wind-down or restructuring notice.
notes: Solicitation vehicles: Mission Office programs, Initiatives & Sprints, and ISOs (Innovative Solutions Openings). ARPANET-H is the ecosystem/network. Status verified 2026-09-17. Award figures are not stated at this level and remain unconfirmed; the agency directs applicants to individual solicitations.

program_name: Early Career Faculty (ECF) — Space Technology Research Grants (STRG)
stated_purpose: Supports outstanding untenured early-career faculty to pursue high-priority, low-TRL space-technology research; part of the Space Technology Research Grants (STRG) program within NASA's Space Technology Mission Directorate (STMD).
design_notes: coverage_type=guidance because this represents NASA's family of early-career-faculty research lines (STMD ECF plus discipline New Investigator Program lines) rather than a single perpetual solicitation; topics rotate annually. ECF confirmed as a funded STRG activity on NASA's own STRG page. ECF25-specific figures (>=$750K floor, ~6 awards) come from the most recent solicitation on NSPIRES. research_stage=exploratory_highrisk reflects low-TRL space-tech focus.
typical_award_size: >=$750,000 total (ECF25 floor) over the award period (~$250K/yr over ~3 yr)
eligibility_window: untenured, tenure-track assistant professor at the sponsoring US university at time of award
specific_topic: space technology (annual STMD-defined topic areas; e.g., entry diagnostics, autonomous spacecraft GN&C)
prior_funding_exclusion: gated by untenured-assistant-professor status rather than years since degree; one proposal per PI per solicitation.
eligibility_notes: PI must be an untenured tenure-track assistant professor and a US citizen or lawful permanent resident at award; only accredited US universities may submit; one proposal per PI, no co-investigators (collaborators allowed, excluding NASA employees).
review_criteria_official: NASA merit review: intrinsic scientific/technical merit of the proposed technology research; relevance to NASA STMD technology objectives/topic areas; and cost reasonableness/realism.
status_evidence: “Early Career Faculty (ECF)” is listed among the current Funded STRG Activities; no suspension notice.
notes: Audit: replaced the simpler.grants.gov (grants.gov aggregator) source_url with NASA's own STRG program page (nasa.gov/about-strg). Distinct from tenure-agnostic ROSES research grants; targets untenured assistant professors specifically.

program_name: FINESST — Future Investigators in NASA Earth and Space Science and Technology
stated_purpose: Awards graduate student-designed research projects that advance the Science Mission Directorate's science, technology, and exploration goals; the graduate student (Future Investigator) has primary initiative to define the project.
design_notes: Training-grant-style fellowship: award goes to the US institution; the graduate student is the Future Investigator and primary author while the advisor is PI-of-record. Runs annually across SMD divisions (Earth Science, Heliophysics, Planetary Science, Astrophysics, Biological & Physical Sciences) via the ROSES solicitation. topic_restricted kept false because eligibility spans NASA's broad science portfolio (mission-relevance filter, not a narrow topic gate).
typical_award_size: up to $50,000 per year (up to ~$150,000 total)
eligibility_window: graduate student (Future Investigator) enrolled at a US institution with sufficient time remaining in the degree
prior_funding_exclusion: a student may hold only one FINESST/NESSF award tied to a single degree pursuit; prior recipients for the same degree are ineligible (per FINESST NOFO).
eligibility_notes: Proposal submitted by an accredited US university (or other eligible org) on behalf of the graduate-student Future Investigator, who must be the primary author; a faculty advisor/mentor serves as PI-of-record. No US-citizenship requirement (unlike NSF GRFP).
review_criteria_official: NASA merit review: intrinsic scientific/technical merit of the proposed research and the Future Investigator's potential; relevance to NASA/SMD science objectives; and reasonableness of the requested budget.
notes: Successor to the NASA Earth and Space Science Fellowship (NESSF); solicited annually within ROSES. Audit: downgraded high->medium — source_url is a 2022 ROSES F.5 amendment (NASA's own domain, so not an aggregator) and the clean /researchers/finesst page 404'd this pass; $50K/yr, 3-yr terms are stable and reissued annually under the current ROSES. SOURCE DEFECT 2026-09-17: source_url points at ROSES-2022 Amendment 70, whose proposals were due 7 February 2023; page last updated 7 August 2023. A historical document cannot establish current status either way. Re-point at the current ROSES cycle's F.5 element and re-check.

stated_purpose: Offers competitive fellowships to early-career scientists to conduct independent research in collaboration with a NASA advisor at a NASA center or affiliated institution.
design_notes: Administered for NASA by ORAU (official program site). Three review cycles per year (Mar 1, Jul 1, Nov 1) — cadence marked annual (recurring) with cycles noted. Split from the Senior Fellowship variant because career stage and stipend determination differ (filterable).
typical_award_size: stipend from $70,000/year (locality/field supplements possible) + $10,000/year travel; NASA covers ~85% of health-insurance premium
eligibility_window: held a doctoral degree for less than 5 years at appointment start
prior_funding_exclusion: yes: cannot begin a new NPP appointment within 5 years of concluding a prior NPP fellowship.
eligibility_notes: US citizens, lawful permanent residents, and foreign nationals eligible for J-1 Exchange Visitor status (J-1 must be obtained before starting if selected); also LPR/asylee/refugee applicants with valid EAD and pending I-485/I-589. Must relocate to and reside at the NASA center/advisor location. Stipend ($70k start), $10k travel, and ~85% health-premium coverage confirmed on the NPP benefits page.
review_criteria_official: Discipline-panel merit review: quality/originality and feasibility of the proposed research, applicant qualifications, and the match with the NASA advisor and center.
status_evidence: “November 2026 cycle is open. View current opportunities.”
notes: Three fixed review cycles per year. Full-time; no concurrent outside employment permitted. Audit: $70k stipend, $10k travel, 85% health, and <5yr window re-confirmed on funder page.

stated_purpose: Provides fellowships for experienced researchers (five or more years past the doctorate) to conduct independent research with a NASA advisor.
design_notes: Split from the Postdoctoral Fellowship variant on career stage (5+ years since PhD) and stipend basis. Same program, application system (ORAU), and three annual cycles.
typical_award_size: stipend set by location, years of experience beyond the doctorate, and career achievements (above the postdoctoral base) + $10,000/year travel
eligibility_window: held a doctoral degree for 5 or more years
prior_funding_exclusion: yes: cannot begin a new NPP appointment within 5 years of concluding a prior NPP fellowship.
eligibility_notes: Same citizenship/residency and residency-relocation rules as the postdoctoral tier (US citizens, LPRs, J-1-eligible foreign nationals). Distinguished from the postdoctoral tier only by 5+ years since the doctorate and a higher, experience-based stipend. Individually-determined senior stipend confirmed on the NPP benefits page.
review_criteria_official: Discipline-panel merit review: quality/originality and feasibility of the proposed research, applicant qualifications, and the match with the NASA advisor and center.
status_evidence: “November 2026 cycle is open. View current opportunities.”
notes: A separate NPP Management Fellowship track (requires >=1 year in a research fellowship) also exists; not enumerated here.

funder: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
stated_purpose: Provides two-year appointments for recent doctoral recipients to conduct independent research in association with NIST staff, administered through the National Academies' NRC Research Associateship Programs.
design_notes: Individual postdoctoral fellowship hosted at NIST; adviser must be secured pre-application. Two fixed application periods per year (Feb 1 and Aug 1). US-citizen-only gate is stricter than most (no PR); mapped to citizen_national_pr_required (nearest enum) with the citizen-only restriction flagged in eligibility_notes. Citizenship, PhD<5yr, GS-11 stipend, 2-yr duration, and Feb/Aug cycles all re-confirmed on the funder page.
typical_award_size: stipend equivalent to GS-11 step 1 for the Washington, DC metro area (~$72,000+ est., locality-adjusted)
eligibility_window: held the PhD (STEM discipline) for less than 5 years
prior_funding_exclusion: must have held the PhD less than 5 years and be a US citizen; no separate prior-award disqualifier stated.
eligibility_notes: Must be a US citizen — permanent residents are NOT eligible for this program (confirmed on the NIST page). PhD held less than 5 years in a science/engineering/math discipline. Applicants must identify and contact a prospective NIST adviser before applying; Selective Service registration required where applicable.
review_criteria_official: National Academies' NRC panel review: scientific/technical merit of the proposed research and the applicant's qualifications and promise, plus the adviser/research-opportunity match.
status_evidence: NIST: “we are waiting for more guidance before notifying selected applicants”, with applicants told to “regularly check this website for the latest information and updates”. Not accepting new applications pending internal guidance, and no reopening date is given — only the historical 1 February / 1 August deadlines.
notes: Disciplines: chemistry, physics, materials science, math, computer science, engineering. Two review cycles per year.

funder: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
stated_purpose: Provides hands-on research experiences at NIST for students, recent graduates, postdocs, and faculty, strengthening the STEM workforce and NIST's measurement-science mission.
design_notes: PREP is structured as 5-year cooperative agreements between NIST and partner universities; individuals are hired into research-associate appointments via posted vacancies (submission_path=other; institution_type=other = PREP partner universities only). mechanism_type=training_grant captures the workforce-development appointment at the individual level. Multi-stage career eligibility.
typical_award_size: stipend/salary varies by level (undergraduate through postdoctoral/faculty); specific amounts unspecified on program page
typical_duration: varies by appointment (within the 5-year institutional cooperative agreement)
eligibility_window: undergraduate, graduate, recent graduate, postdoctoral, senior researcher, or faculty affiliated with a PREP partner university
prior_funding_exclusion: none stated.
eligibility_notes: Open to US citizens and foreign nationals with appropriate visa to work at NIST. Applicants apply to advertised vacancies through PREP partner/associate universities (e.g., Boulder CO, Gaithersburg MD, Charleston SC hubs).
review_criteria_official: Selection by NIST research units against posted position/vacancy requirements (research fit, qualifications); managed through partner-university cooperative agreements.
status_evidence: Page updated 2 September 2026 with live application links for the Boulder and Gaithersburg participating universities; no suspension notice.
notes: Not a nationally open individual competition — access is via affiliated PREP universities' vacancy postings.

funder: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
stated_purpose: Provides undergraduate students a paid summer research experience working alongside NIST scientists and engineers.
design_notes: Individual undergraduate summer fellowship; applications submitted through USAJobs. 2026 stipend figures ($710/wk = $7,810; up to $4,500 housing; up to $500 travel) re-confirmed on the funder page; adjusts yearly.
typical_award_size: $7,810 for the 11-week summer stipend ($710/week) + up to $4,500 housing assistance + up to $500 travel (2026)
eligibility_window: full-time undergraduate at an accredited US 2- or 4-year college (first-years through graduating seniors); age 18+
prior_funding_exclusion: none.
eligibility_notes: Must be a US citizen or permanent resident (with proof). Six NIST laboratories participate. Apply via USAJobs. 2026 stipend/housing/travel figures and citizenship confirmed on nist.gov/surf.
review_criteria_official: Selection by NIST laboratories on academic record, statement of interest, references, and fit with available research projects.
status_evidence: “vacancy announcement expected to open USAjobs mid-October 2026” with “applications due at the end of January 2027”.
notes: Participating labs: Communications Technology, Engineering, Information Technology, Material Measurement, Physical Measurement, plus NIST Center for Neutron Research.

stated_purpose: Provide mentored research career development to a junior-faculty research scientist who is a citizen of, and committed to research at, an institution in a low- or middle-income country (LMIC).
design_notes: Federal U.S. funder (NIH/Fogarty) but the awardee institution is a foreign LMIC organization — hence host_country_institution_required and institution_type 'other'.
typical_award_size: Salary/research-development support scaled to LMIC context (varies) (est.)
eligibility_window: Applicant is an LMIC citizen with a master's/doctoral degree, holds a junior-faculty appointment, and is employed by an eligible LMIC academic/research institution (the applicant organization is a foreign LMIC institution). No U.S. citizenship requirement.
specific_topic: Global-health research relevant to low- and middle-income countries (Fogarty International Center)
prior_funding_exclusion: yes (mentored career-development stage): for early-career scientists not yet holding a major independent research award; applicant must need additional mentored research experience. Specific disqualifiers per the current Fogarty K43 NOFO.
eligibility_notes: Standing Fogarty program; specific parent NOFOs are periodically reissued (between-cycle status can vary).
review_criteria_official: Mentored-K criteria adapted for global settings (traditional K structure): Candidate; Career Development Plan; Research Plan; Mentor(s)/Collaborators; Environment & Institutional Commitment (LMIC institution).
status_evidence: Activity code K43 (“Emerging Global Leader Award”) is listed in NIH's activity-code index as of 2026-09-17, with no retirement or archive notice.

stated_purpose: Provide extended, stable funding to accomplished cancer researchers with outstanding records, enabling ambitious, flexible, long-horizon programs of cancer research.
typical_award_size: Up to $600,000 direct costs/yr
eligibility_window: For established investigators with an outstanding record of cancer-research productivity and substantial current NCI research funding as PD/PI; not for early-career investigators.
specific_topic: Cancer research (NCI mission)
prior_funding_exclusion: yes (inverted): requires a strong record of substantial, current NCI/NIH research support as PD/PI; intended to consolidate/replace existing project grants with one stable award. Not open to those without an accomplished independently funded track record.
eligibility_notes: NCI encourages nominations across career stages including women and underrepresented groups, but the current cancer.gov page frames this as encouragement, NOT an eligibility gate or scoring preference (post-SFFA-consistent); hence identity_gate_type n/a.
review_criteria_official: NIH simplified 3-factor framework focused on the investigator's overall program, track record, and transformative potential (Importance; Rigor & Feasibility; Expertise & Resources).
status_evidence: Activity code R35 (“Outstanding Investigator Award”) is listed in NIH's activity-code index as of 2026-09-17, with no retirement or archive notice.

program_name: NIGMS Maximizing Investigators' Research Award (MIRA, R35)
stated_purpose: Provide a single, consolidated, stable grant supporting the full program of research in an investigator's lab within the NIGMS mission, increasing flexibility and distributing funding more broadly.
typical_award_size: ESI ~$250,000; New Investigator ~$275,000; Established up to $750,000 direct costs/yr (investigators with ≥$400k NIGMS funding typically ~12% below historical) (est.)
eligibility_window: Separate NOFOs: Established/New Investigators (PAR-26-121) and Early Stage Investigators (PAR-27-032). EI/NI generally need ≥1 NIGMS single-PI R01-equivalent (R01/R37/DP1/DP2/SC1) or current MIRA; ESI variant open without prior NIGMS support (ESI = within 10 yrs of terminal degree).
specific_topic: NIGMS basic-biomedical mission (no disease-specific focus)
prior_funding_exclusion: yes (mutually exclusive with other NIGMS support): all other NIGMS research grants are terminated upon MIRA issuance; may not have a MIRA plus another NIGMS RPG (R01/R15/R21/R37) pending simultaneously; PI must devote ≥45% of total research effort to the MIRA.
eligibility_notes: 5-year single-PI award; renewable. ESI/New-Investigator entry point makes it a de facto first independent award for many NIGMS-funded labs. NOFO numbers PAR-26-121 / PAR-27-032 confirmed on NIGMS MIRA page (updated 2026-07-24).
review_criteria_official: NIH simplified 3-factor framework applied at the level of the investigator's overall research program (Importance; Rigor & Feasibility; Expertise & Resources), with emphasis on track record and potential.
status_evidence: PAR-26-121 — applications accepted 2026-2028 (established/new investigators); PAR-27-032 — accepted through 6 February 2029 (early-stage investigators).
notes: Re-verified 2026-09-17: 'MIRA grants will generally be for 5 years, for both established investigators/new investigators and early stage investigators.' The page states duration but no dollar figures, so the recorded amounts were not confirmed this run.

program_name: NIH Center & Program Project Grants (P01 / P30 / P50)
stated_purpose: Support multi-component, thematically integrated research: P01 program projects (multiple interrelated projects + shared cores), P50 specialized/disease centers (research + cores), and P30 center core grants (shared resources/cores supporting a base of NIH-funded investigators).
design_notes: P30 (center core) is infrastructure_resource in intent; P01/P50 are coordinated multi-project research. Collapsed into one center/program-project row to keep the mechanism catalog within scope, variants noted.
typical_award_size: Large, multi-component budgets (vary widely by IC and NOFO)
prior_funding_exclusion: no (institution/PD-led; eligibility per NOFO). Individual project/core leaders vary.
eligibility_notes: Three P-series activity codes collapsed. P30 is primarily infrastructure/shared-core support; P01 and P50 combine research projects with cores. Usually RFA/PAR-driven.
review_criteria_official: Multi-component review: overall program impact plus separate evaluation of each project and core, leadership/synergy, and (for P30) the quality and value of shared resources to the funded user base.
status_evidence: Activity code P01/P30/P50 (“Research Program Projects and Centers”) is listed in NIH's activity-code index as of 2026-09-17, with no retirement or archive notice.

program_name: NIH Clinical Trial / Research Planning Grant (R34)
stated_purpose: Support planning and development activities — team assembly, protocol/design finalization, operations/data-management tools, and feasibility data — that lead to a subsequent full clinical trial or research project.
typical_award_size: Up to $225,000 direct costs/yr; up to $450,000 total (varies by IC)
prior_funding_exclusion: no. Not renewable (one-time planning award).
eligibility_notes: 3 standard cycles/yr; modular budgets (except foreign). Permits early peer review of a trial's rationale/concept.
review_criteria_official: NIH simplified 3-factor framework applied to the planning aims (Importance; Rigor & Feasibility of the planning plan; Expertise & Resources).
status_evidence: Activity code R34 (“Planning Grant”) is listed in NIH's activity-code index as of 2026-09-17, with no retirement or archive notice.

stated_purpose: Enable exceptional junior scientists to skip the traditional postdoc and move immediately into an independent research position (NIH Common Fund High-Risk, High-Reward).
typical_award_size: $250,000 direct costs/yr
eligibility_window: Applicants from 16 months before to 12 months after receipt of a doctoral degree or end of post-graduate clinical training; must be in a non-independent position at application.
prior_funding_exclusion: yes: for individuals who have NOT yet moved into an independent position and are within the tight early-independence window; enables bypassing postdoctoral training.
eligibility_notes: Institutions are limited to 2 applications per year (limited submission). One receipt date per year.
review_criteria_official: Common Fund HRHR specialized review emphasizing the candidate's exceptional promise, readiness for independence, and the host institution's commitment.
status_evidence: Activity code DP5 is listed in NIH's activity-code index; the programme page reads “No open funding announcements … information about future announcements.” Between cycles, no termination notice.

stated_purpose: Support unusually creative Early Stage Investigators proposing innovative, high-impact projects (NIH Common Fund High-Risk, High-Reward), without requiring extensive preliminary data.
typical_award_size: $475,000 direct costs/yr; up to $2,375,000 total direct costs over the 5-year award (per current RFA-RM-27-002)
eligibility_window: Early Stage Investigators only (within 10 years of terminal degree and no prior R01-equivalent NIH award); single PD/PI; ≥25% research effort.
prior_funding_exclusion: yes (ESI gate): must not have received an R01-equivalent or other substantial NIH independent research award; ESI status required.
eligibility_notes: One receipt date per year.
review_criteria_official: Common Fund HRHR specialized review emphasizing innovation/creativity and ESI potential; multi-stage editorial-board review (not standard study-section criteria).
status_evidence: Activity code DP2 is listed in NIH's activity-code index; the programme page reads “No open funding announcements. Check the funding opportunities page for past announcements and information about future announcements.” Between cycles, no termination notice.

stated_purpose: Support individual scientists of exceptional creativity who propose pioneering, potentially transformative approaches to major challenges in biomedical/behavioral/social science (NIH Common Fund High-Risk, High-Reward).
typical_award_size: $700,000 direct costs/yr (up to $3.5M direct costs over 5 years)
eligibility_window: Open to all career stages (single PD/PI); requires ≥51% research effort in years 1-3 (stepping down in years 4-5); must propose a new research direction.
prior_funding_exclusion: no (holding other NIH support is allowed); single-PI, new-direction requirement.
eligibility_notes: One receipt date per year. High-Risk, High-Reward program.
review_criteria_official: Common Fund HRHR specialized review: emphasis on the significance/transformative potential of the idea and the investigator's creativity and track record; multi-stage editorial-board review with possible finalist interviews (not standard study-section criteria).
review_signals_informal: Community knowledge: bold vision and investigator creativity weigh more than detailed preliminary data; finalist interviews can matter (confidence low).
status_evidence: 'No open funding announcements. Check the funding opportunities page for past announcements and information about future announcements.' Between cycles, with no termination notice — active under D-009.
notes: Award re-verified 2026-09-17: '$700,000 in direct costs per year for up to 5 years' — matches.

stated_purpose: Support early-stage, exploratory or developmental, higher-risk research — novel approaches, feasibility, or new methods — where preliminary data may be limited.
typical_award_size: Up to $275,000 direct costs total over 2 years (no more than $200,000 in any single year)
prior_funding_exclusion: no (preliminary data not required; open to all career stages). Not intended for large or extended projects.
eligibility_notes: 3 standard cycles/yr. Not renewable as an R21.
review_criteria_official: NIH simplified 3-factor framework (Importance; Rigor & Feasibility; Expertise & Resources).
status_evidence: Activity code R21 (“Exploratory/Developmental Research Grant”) is listed in NIH's activity-code index as of 2026-09-17, with no retirement or archive notice.

program_name: NIH Institutional Research Training Grant (Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA T32)
stated_purpose: Enable institutions to develop or enhance research-training opportunities and to appoint predoctoral and/or postdoctoral trainees to structured programs in areas of NIH-mission need.
typical_award_size: Trainee stipends + tuition/fees + training-related expenses + institutional allowance (per appointed slot)
eligibility_window: The INSTITUTION (via a program director/faculty) applies; appointed trainees must be U.S. citizens, non-citizen nationals, or permanent residents.
prior_funding_exclusion: n/a at the grant level; individual trainees are subject to NRSA aggregate support limits (5 yrs predoctoral / 3 yrs postdoctoral across institutional + individual awards) and NRSA payback/service provisions.
eligibility_notes: Institutional award; program director assembles faculty, trainees, curriculum. Trainee-citizenship gate is the notable restriction.
review_criteria_official: Institutional training-grant criteria (revised): Training Program & Environment; Program Director(s)/Faculty; Trainees & Recruitment; Training Record & Evaluation.
status_evidence: Activity code T32 (“Institutional National Research Service Award”) is listed in NIH's activity-code index as of 2026-09-17, with no retirement or archive notice.

stated_purpose: Repay qualified educational debt for doctoral-level researchers who commit to NIH mission-relevant research, helping recruit and retain health-research talent.
design_notes: Not a research project grant — an individual loan-repayment benefit. Multiple topic-specific subprograms collapsed to one row per dataset guidance.
typical_award_size: Up to $50,000/yr of qualified educational debt repayment (confirmed current on grants.nih.gov LRP award page; plus tax offset)
eligibility_window: Doctoral-level degree; U.S. citizen/national/permanent resident; qualified educational debt ≥~20% of institutional base salary; engaged ≥20 hrs/week in qualifying research funded by a domestic nonprofit/university/government entity; not a federal employee.
specific_topic: Extramural research-focus subprograms (Clinical; Pediatric; Health Disparities; Contraception & Infertility; Emerging Areas/REACH)
prior_funding_exclusion: does not require holding an NIH research grant; excludes federal employees and debt already covered by other loan-repayment obligations; research must be nonprofit/government-supported.

program_name: Research Supplements to Promote Re-entry, Re-integration into, and Re-training in Health-Related (Biomedical and Behavioral) Research Careers - Re-entry component
funder: National Institutes of Health (NIH); led by the Office of Research on Women's Health (ORWH) and administered by participating Institutes/Centers (e.g., NHLBI, NCI, NIA, NIDA, NIGMS, NINDS)
stated_purpose: Provides administrative supplements to active NIH research grants to support individuals with high potential to re-enter an active biomedical or behavioral research career after a qualifying interruption (family/caregiving, illness or injury, relocation, debt-driven non-research work, emergency job loss, or military service) through a mentored research training experience.
design_notes: Administrative supplement to an existing active NIH research grant (parent Administrative Supplement PA-20-272, now the PA-26-001 lineage), NOT a standalone award: the re-entering scientist is added to a current PI's active grant. The umbrella NOSI historically bundled three distinct tracks - Re-entry (return after interruption), Re-integration (leaving unsafe/discriminatory research environments), and Re-training (acquiring new skills). NIH restructured in 2025: combined NOSI NOT-OD-23-170 had its expiration pulled forward to 09/09/2025, and Institutes now present Re-entry separately (e.g., NHLBI posts 'Re-Entry' pages split by career level, dropping the re-integration/re-training branding).
typical_award_size: Salary plus fringe at the NIH-appropriate level plus a modest research allowance (e.g., NHLBI: up to $6,000/yr supplies and travel and up to $1,000/yr for scientific meetings); total varies by Institute/Center and the host grant
typical_duration: 1 to 3 years (up to the remaining project period of the parent grant)
eligibility_window: Career interruption of at least 6 months (1 year at some Institutes) and no more than 8 years; candidate must have been in an advanced postdoctoral or investigator-level position at the time of the interruption
prior_funding_exclusion: Requires an existing active NIH research grant to host the supplement (the mechanism is itself a supplement to current NIH funding); the re-entering candidate must not currently hold independent research support and generally cannot be a current PD/PI on an NIH research award.
eligibility_notes: The re-entering individual must hold a doctoral (or equivalent) degree with prior advanced-postdoc or investigator-level experience, must not currently be engaged in full-time paid research, and applies through a mentor/PI who holds an active, eligible NIH research grant with sufficient time remaining. Qualifying interruption reasons include childcare/family responsibilities, illness or injury, relocation, debt-driven non-research work, emergency job loss (e.g., COVID-19), and military service.
review_criteria_official: Administrative (non-peer) IC review of the candidate's potential to re-enter an independent research career, the quality and appropriateness of the mentored training plan, and relevance to the parent grant and the Institute's mission
review_signals_informal: A strong, well-funded host lab/mentor with an active parent grant; a credible time-limited plan to return to independent research; clear documentation of the qualifying interruption
notes: Last umbrella NOSI NOT-OD-23-170 (released 09/06/2023) had its expiration moved up to 09/09/2025; a reissued umbrella NOSI was not locatable in the NIH Guide as of the checked date. The program remains active and is administered by individual Institutes/Centers via IC-specific guidelines tied to the parent Administrative Supplement PA. Confirm the current IC notice with the target Institute before applying. An expired notice says the announcement lapsed, not that the programme ended, so status stays unknown. Re-point at the current re-entry supplement notice and re-check.

program_name: Institution-administered Re-Entry Postdoctoral Research Program (representative example: Harvard Catalyst Re-Entry Research Supplement)
funder: Harvard Catalyst, The Harvard Clinical and Translational Science Center (representative named example; underlying funds from the NIH/NCATS CTSA award)
stated_purpose: Supports doctoral-level researchers returning to clinical/translational research after a career interruption (childrearing, illness in self or family, relocation, debt-driven non-research work, or military service) through a mentored, institution-administered re-entry research supplement.
design_notes: GUIDANCE ROW representing the U.S. pattern of institution-administered re-entry postdoctoral programs. In the U.S. these are generally NOT standalone institution-funded fellowships; they are typically local implementations of the NIH/NCATS CTSA re-entry supplement run by a university's CTSA hub (Harvard Catalyst shown as a named representative). The candidate submits a Letter of Intent to the hub, which invites full proposals routed to NIH as administrative supplements to the CTSA parent grant. The 'institutional' label reflects administration/host, not the (federal CTSA) funding source.
typical_award_size: Salary support up to about $100,000/yr plus fringe, and about $10,000 for supplies/travel/publication (Harvard Catalyst figures; varies by institution)
typical_duration: Up to about 2 years (up to 12 person-months; 1-year projects also considered)
eligibility_window: Career interruption of at least 1 year and no more than 8 years; previously in a postdoctoral or faculty position; minimum 50% time commitment to the re-entry effort
prior_funding_exclusion: Candidate should not currently hold independent research funding; the mechanism is a supplement to the institution's active federal (CTSA) award
eligibility_notes: Availability is institution-specific and cyclical; applicants must be affiliated with (or recruited to) the administering university. As of the checked date, Harvard Catalyst's re-entry LOI cycle was closed - confirm current availability with the specific institution's CTSA hub or office of postdoctoral affairs.
review_criteria_official: Institution/hub review of the candidate's re-entry potential, the mentored research/training plan, the mentor and environment, and alignment with the CTSA parent grant; finalists are routed to NIH for administrative approval
review_signals_informal: Strong mentor and departmental commitment; a feasible plan to re-establish an independent research trajectory; documented qualifying interruption
notes: Representative anchor only. Standalone, purely institution-funded U.S. re-entry postdoctoral fellowships are rare and not standardized; most 'institutional re-entry postdoc' opportunities are university-administered NIH/CTSA re-entry supplements, offered by CTSA hubs across academic medical centers. Harvard Catalyst's LOI form was closed at the checked date, so treat availability as cyclical/institution-dependent. (Robust standalone re-entry fellowships exist in the UK - e.g., Wellcome/Daphne Jackson - but are out of U.S. scope.)

The voucher/subsidy pays for USE of institutional core-facility instruments and staff time (anchor explicitly excludes consumables/specialty chemicals). Applicant develops a budget with the core manager and submits a short narrative to the research office. Purpose is to develop new methods or generate preliminary data for extramural proposals.

notes: Requires the institution to operate shared core facilities (research-intensive universities/AMCs); many voucher programs are seeded by CTSA hubs or NIH S10/core grants. program_name: CTSA intramural pilot / translational pilot awards
funder: Home institution (US universities & academic medical centers)

IMPORTANT classification note: although the CTSA hub is backed by an NIH/NCATS UM1/UL1 cooperative agreement, the PILOT AWARD itself is administered INTRAMURALLY by the institution's CTSI to its own investigators, so funder_category=institutional and mechanism_type=seed_pilot (not cooperative_agreement, which describes the parent NCATS award to the hub).
typical_award_size: ~$20k-$50k (est.); corroborating anchor (Case Western CTSC) up to $50k each; some hubs award up to ~$100k. (UF CTSI page confirms the mechanism but does not publish a per-award dollar figure.)

eligibility_notes: Gate is being an NIH-PI-eligible faculty member at an institution with a CTSA hub. Investigators apply through the local CTSI/CTSC (often via LOI -> design studio -> full application). Human/animal work needs IRB/IACUC (and NIH prior approval) before start. Intended to produce preliminary data and reusable translational tools/methods that seed extramural (often R-level) applications.

notes: Available only at the ~60 institutions with an NCATS CTSA hub (academic medical centers), hence institution_type_restriction=r1_or_equiv. Scope is clinical & translational science broadly (not a single disease), so topic_restricted=false. prior_funding_exclusion: no formal prior-award gate; eligibility is bounded by early-postdoc career stage (typically within ~5 yrs of PhD; some programs limit prior postdoc experience).
eligibility_notes: Gate is holding (or taking up) the fellowship as a postdoc appointee at the institution; nationality generally not restricted. Applicants apply directly, usually naming a prospective faculty mentor/host unit. Explicit aim is to build the future tenure-track faculty pipeline. Anchor (U-M President's Postdoc) for AY25-26 limited hosting to five named schools (Dentistry; Environment & Sustainability; Information; Nursing; Social Work); scope varies yearly and by campus.
review_criteria_official: Research promise/quality, fit with a faculty mentor and host unit, and potential for a future faculty career; PPFP-family programs also weigh holistic contributions to diversity/equal opportunity (perspective-based, not demographic).
status_evidence: On-line application opened 09.01.2026 and closes 11.01.2026 (U-M President's Postdoctoral Fellowship, the named exemplar for this guidance row).
notes: Identity fields reflect the President's/Provost's (PPFP-model) SUBSET as VERIFIED on the anchor page 2026-07: U-M expresses interest in scholars who bring a critical perspective from a 'non-traditional educational background or understanding of the experiences of groups historically underrepresented in higher education' and weighs contributions to diversity/equal opportunity as a HOLISTIC, non-demographic factor. This is a SOFT preference (prioritizes), NOT a demographic gate; post-SFFA (2023) the language is explicitly contribution/perspective-based, not identity-restricted. Downgraded from the prior [URM, first_generation] stamp: dropped 'first_generation' (not supported by the current non-demographic wording), retained URM as the closest filterable mapping of 'groups historically underrepresented.' Generic departmental/provost postdoc fellowships carry no identity criteria (identity_gate_type = n/a). confidence low on the identity and stipend fields specifically.

funder: Home institution (US universities & academic medical centers)
stated_purpose: Sustain a full-time faculty member's independent research program during a temporary loss of significant funding, usually between two extramural (R01-equivalent) grants (anchor: UCSF).
design_notes: Representative anchor: UCSF School of Medicine Bridge Funding Program (verified 2026-07: <=$150k, <=12 mo, requires recent well-scored unfunded federal application, 25% dept match, cannot reapply until 6 mo after prior award). GUIDANCE row for the bridge/gap-funding TYPE (also at Oregon, Purdue, FSU, Wisconsin, Cincinnati, IU). mechanism_type=research_grant proxy: this is stopgap funding to sustain a mature lab/personnel between grants, NOT a seed/pilot. Note the qualifying condition is INVERSE of a prior-funding exclusion: you must HAVE HAD extramural funding and a scored unfunded resubmission to qualify.
typical_award_size: ~$25k-$150k (est.); anchor (UCSF School of Medicine) caps at $150k, with the department providing 25% of the award.
eligibility_window: During a funding gap; anchor requires >3 years as full-time salaried faculty and a recent well-scored-but-unfunded federal application.
prior_funding_exclusion: no (inverse requirement): eligibility REQUIRES prior/lapsing extramural funding plus a recent well-scored but unfunded federal application; having no external-funding history typically disqualifies. (Anchor nuance: New Investigators still holding a mentored K award are ineligible.)
eligibility_notes: Gate is being an established, full-time faculty PI at the institution experiencing a temporary loss of significant extramural support. Anchor priority tiers: Established Investigators (8+ yrs faculty, documented 3 yrs continuous peer-reviewed support, losing/anticipating loss of >40% of extramural funding) and New Investigators (<=8 yrs faculty with independent programs; those still holding a mentored K are ineligible). Department chair must document a financial commitment (anchor: 25% match). Faculty apply to the school/research office (anchor: two cycles/yr, Winter and Summer).
review_criteria_official: Institutional committee: strength/percentile of the recent unfunded federal application, research program independence, likelihood of near-term recovery of extramural funding, productivity, and documented department commitment/match.
notes: Most common at academic medical centers and wet-lab-intensive units where a grant lapse threatens salaried personnel; campus-wide (domain-agnostic) versions also exist. Cadence framed rolling because need is unpredictable, though anchor runs fixed Winter/Summer cycles; department cost-share is common.

funder: Home institution (US universities & academic medical centers)
stated_purpose: Jump-start worthwhile new projects with short-term, one-time internal support to generate preliminary data for external proposals (anchor language: 'jump-start worthwhile projects by providing short-term, one-time support').
design_notes: Representative anchor: University of Arizona Research Office Faculty Seed Grants (verified 2026-07: up to $15k, Track 1 assistant / Track 2 associate profs, annual, one award per PI per 4 yrs, must lead to data for new external proposals). GUIDANCE row for the near-universal internal-seed-grant TYPE; amounts/terms are set per-institution. Corroborating index: UChicago Office of Research internal-funding catalog. Leveraging preliminary data into extramural funding is the explicit intent.
typical_award_size: ~$10k-$75k (est.); anchor (Arizona Faculty Seed Grants) up to $15k one-time (single-investigator).
typical_duration: ~6-18 months (est.); anchor is a 1-year award period.
eligibility_window: Open to faculty; anchor limits to one award per PI every 4 years and splits Track 1 (assistant profs / early career) / Track 2 (associate profs / mid-career).
prior_funding_exclusion: no formal PI-history gate; programs typically target NEW directions/preliminary data and often cap repeat awards (anchor: one per PI per 4 yrs).
eligibility_notes: Gate is faculty appointment at the institution. Faculty apply directly through the research office's internal-funding portal (anchor: 'Arizona Cultivate'). Intended to generate preliminary/pilot data or scholarly/creative output that seeds a new EXTERNAL proposal. Some campuses open these to all ranks or to interdisciplinary teams.
review_criteria_official: Institutional review: scientific/scholarly merit and likelihood of leading to competitive external funding or significant scholarship.
notes: Names vary (seed grant, pilot grant, faculty research grant, university research council award, interdisciplinary seed). Larger interdisciplinary/team seed programs reach the upper (~$50k-$75k) end. Some are rolling rather than annual.

funder: Home institution (US universities & academic medical centers)
stated_purpose: Internally select the institution's nominee(s) for external programs that limit the number of applications a single institution may submit, ensuring compliance and maximizing competitiveness (anchor: UMN RIO).
design_notes: Representative anchor: University of Minnesota Research & Innovation Office Limited Submissions Program (verified 2026-07; corroborated by UChicago, Ohio State, Cornell, Rochester, Iowa). GUIDANCE row: near-universal at research universities. mechanism_type=research_grant is a proxy - this row represents the internal LIMITED-SUBMISSION NOMINATION PROCESS itself (a gatekeeping mechanism), not a funding award. submission_path=institutional_nomination_limited is the defining field. Underlying external awards span research grants, instrumentation (NSF MRI, NIH S10), center/training grants, and foundation prizes.
typical_award_size: n/a - this is an internal nomination GATEWAY, not itself a purse; the eventual award is the external sponsor's (varies widely, from ~$50k foundation awards to multi-$M instrumentation/center grants).
typical_duration: n/a (gateway process); underlying external award duration varies.
eligibility_window: Whenever a capped external opportunity is posted; anyone eligible for that external program may enter the internal competition.
prior_funding_exclusion: n/a (nomination process; any prior-funding limits come from the downstream external program, not the internal competition).
eligibility_notes: Gate is being an eligible PI at the institution for an external program that caps the number of applications per institution. The research-development office posts the opportunity, collects short internal pre-proposals, convenes a faculty/associate-dean review panel when entries exceed the funder's cap, and the VP for Research selects the nominee(s). Anchor rule (UMN RIO), verified 2026-07: 'Approval from RIO must be obtained before applying to a limited submission opportunity,' and proposals 'should not be submitted to any limited submission opportunities without going through the UMN limited submission process.'
review_criteria_official: Internal panel scores on scientific merit, fit to the sponsor's stated criteria, and alignment with institutional strategic priorities; the VP for Research makes the final nomination.
notes: Not a source of institutional money - it allocates the scarce right to APPLY externally. Included because submission_path=institutional_nomination_limited is a distinct, filterable access pattern researchers must navigate. Cadence is rolling because opportunities post throughout the year, usually ~3 months before the sponsor deadline.

stated_purpose: Fund academic research aligned with Amazon's areas of interest via one-time unrestricted cash gifts and AWS Promotional Credits.
design_notes: Cash awards are structured as one-time UNRESTRICTED GIFTS to the PI's institution (not grants/contracts), often paired with AWS Promotional Credits. Multiple topic-specific calls per year, hence irregular cadence. AUDIT 2026-07-18: program rules confirm the unrestricted-gift + AWS-credit structure, one-proposal-per-call limit, and that dollar amounts are set at Amazon's sole discretion (undisclosed).
typical_award_size: One-time unrestricted cash gift to the institution plus AWS Promotional Credits; all amounts determined by Amazon in its sole discretion and not disclosed on the funder page (historically up to ~$100k total incl. credits (est.))
eligibility_window: Full-time faculty at an accredited academic institution (or permanent researcher at a qualifying nonprofit)
specific_topic: Multiple research areas incl. ML, computer vision, robotics, sustainability, security/privacy, conversational AI, automated reasoning
prior_funding_exclusion: no: no prior-award exclusion, but limited to one proposal per call period
eligibility_notes: PI must be full-time faculty at an accredited institution (or permanent researcher at a 501(c)(3)-equivalent NGO); one proposal per call period. Void in sanctioned jurisdictions. No Amazon employment in the preceding 12 months; no immediate family/household of Amazon employees; no Amazon cloud-procurement decision authority. Confirmed on funder page.
review_criteria_official: Fit to the call's research area and scientific merit; reviewed by Amazon scientists (specific rubric not published).
notes: Research areas include ML, computer vision, robotics, sustainability, security/privacy/abuse prevention, conversational AI, and automated reasoning. Founded 2015; merged with AWS ML Research Awards in 2020.

stated_purpose: Support emerging leaders in AI/ML research through funding as they pursue their PhDs.
design_notes: Award amount and duration are not publicly disclosed on Apple's page (confidence medium). Nomination via invited universities only. AUDIT 2026-07-18: 2026 recipients page confirms the program is active (seventh year), university-nominated, and open to invited institutions; monetary amount genuinely undisclosed.
typical_award_size: unspecified (fellowship funding toward PhD research; amount not published by Apple)
eligibility_window: PhD students at invited institutions
specific_topic: Artificial intelligence and machine learning
prior_funding_exclusion: unspecified
eligibility_notes: University-nominated; open only to invited institutions (limited submission at participating schools). Students do not apply directly. Confirmed on funder page (2026 cycle, program's seventh year).
review_criteria_official: Innovative research, leadership, and commitment to advancing the field (per program page).
notes: 2026 focus areas span AI for health, IR/knowledge, ML theory, ML algorithms/architectures, human-centered AI, data-centric AI, privacy-preserving ML, speech/NLP, interactive ML & agents, ethics/fairness, computer vision, accessibility.

funder: Corporate affiliate/consortium members (membership fees to a university center)
stated_purpose: Provide membership-based, largely unrestricted support to a university research center/consortium in exchange for early access to research, faculty/student networking, and recruiting.
design_notes: GUIDANCE row (sourced to Stanford's industrial affiliate programs as a reference). Examples: MIT Industrial Liaison Program; Stanford industrial affiliate programs; NSF I/UCRC centers. Membership fees are typically unrestricted support to the center (non-project-specific), distinguishing them from SRAs (project-specific) and gifts (no return benefit). Fee ranges are estimates. AUDIT 2026-07-18: Stanford page confirms the membership model ('any interested company may join'; members receive facilitated access, meetings, reports, recruiting; fees provide unrestricted support).
typical_award_size: Annual membership fees, commonly ~$25k-$150k per member per year depending on program/tier (est.)
eligibility_window: Faculty/centers at the host institution benefit; any company may join by paying membership fees
prior_funding_exclusion: no
eligibility_notes: Membership-based: corporate members pay annual fees providing largely unrestricted support to a center/lab and receive facilitated access to research programs, faculty and students, annual meetings, reports, and recruiting. Any interested company may join (confirmed on Stanford reference).
review_criteria_official: No competitive review; membership-based access (fee for affiliation).
notes: Also encompasses precompetitive research consortia (multiple companies co-funding a shared research agenda).

program_name: Unrestricted / Restricted Industry Gifts (corporate philanthropy to research)
stated_purpose: Provide philanthropic support to a researcher, unit, or research area with no deliverables and no sponsor control over results.
design_notes: GUIDANCE row (sourced to UCI's gift-vs-grant reference). Classified under mechanism_type=research_grant only as the nearest schema value; substantively it is a philanthropic GIFT (corporate philanthropy), NOT a grant/contract. Accessed via University Advancement, not the sponsored programs office. Amazon Research Awards cash is a real-world award structured as an unrestricted gift. AUDIT 2026-07-18: UCI Office of Research page confirms gift markers (no deliverables/IP, no funder direction, minimal reporting).
typical_award_size: Highly variable, donor/relationship-dependent (est.)
typical_duration: N/A (one-time or pledged; no performance period)
eligibility_window: Any faculty/unit designated by the donor; processed via the institution's advancement/development office
prior_funding_exclusion: no
eligibility_notes: Not competitive; donor-directed. A gift confers NO deliverables, no detailed budget/reporting, no sponsor IP rights, and typically waived/reduced indirect costs. Distinguished from sponsored research by the absence of a defined scope of work and of a return benefit to the funder. Confirmed by UCI reference.
review_criteria_official: No competitive review; donor discretion plus institutional gift-acceptance/compliance review.
notes: Key gift markers: no deliverables, no return benefit to funder, low/no F&A, donor cannot control results.

stated_purpose: Recognize and support outstanding graduate students pursuing doctoral research in computer science and related fields.
design_notes: Global program administered across regions with region-specific eligibility and award amounts; funds are paid to the Fellow's university. Row reflects US/Canada terms for the United States jurisdiction. AUDIT 2026-07-18: funder page confirms $85k/yr, up to 2 years, up to 4 nominees per US/Canada university, and the four stated review criteria.
typical_award_size: US/Canada region: US $85,000 per year toward tuition/fees, living expenses, travel, and equipment (effective 2025 for new recipients; confirmed on funder page)
eligibility_window: US/Canada: must have completed graduate coursework in the PhD by the award year; enrolled full-time for the fellowship duration
specific_topic: Computer science and adjacent research areas (ML, systems, HCI, NLP, quantum, health, security)
prior_funding_exclusion: yes: students already receiving a comparable industry fellowship, and past Google Fellowship recipients, are ineligible; Google employees/household members ineligible
eligibility_notes: Nomination-based; direct student applications not accepted. US/Canada universities may nominate up to 4 students (confirmed on funder page). Eligibility and award amounts vary across global regions; this row reflects the US/Canada region.
review_criteria_official: Strength of the research proposal, research impact, student academic achievements, and leadership potential (essay responses also evaluated in US/Canada, East Asia, Latin America). Confirmed on funder page.
notes: Covered fields: computer architecture; algorithms/optimization; health; HCI; ML & ML foundations; machine perception; NLP; privacy/safety/security; quantum computing; software engineering/PL; systems/networking/cloud.

stated_purpose: Recognize and support outstanding PhD students working in areas of mutual interest to IBM.
design_notes: Faculty-nominated (by invitation) rather than direct student application; award amount and duration are per academic year. AUDIT 2026-07-18: funder page documents the 2025 cycle (Fall 2025 + Spring 2026) with confirmed amounts; program is standing (contrast with Meta, dropped).
typical_award_size: US universities: $40,000 (covers Fall + Spring); international: $6,000-$25,000 by country. Confirmed on funder page.
typical_duration: One academic year (Fall + Spring); reset each cycle
eligibility_window: Nominated within two years of estimated graduation; enrolled full-time over the academic year of the award
specific_topic: IBM focus areas (AI, hybrid cloud, quantum computing, semiconductors/hardware, security)
prior_funding_exclusion: unspecified
eligibility_notes: Faculty nomination required and by invitation only (students cannot self-nominate); nominators must be doctoral faculty. IBM employees/contractors may not nominate. Students at institutions in US-embargoed countries are ineligible. Confirmed on funder page.
review_criteria_official: Alignment with IBM focus areas, potential for research excellence, academic standing, publications, and faculty endorsements.
notes: Focus areas include AI, hybrid cloud, quantum computing, semiconductors/hardware, and security. Recipients often paired with an IBM mentor/internship.

program_name: Industry Sponsored Research Agreements (incl. Master Research Agreements)
funder: Industry sponsors (relationship-driven, via university contracting office)
stated_purpose: Fund a defined scope of research at the university directed toward the sponsor's interests, under a negotiated contract with deliverables, reporting, and IP terms.
design_notes: GUIDANCE row (not a single named program; sourced to MIT OSATT as an authoritative reference). A MASTER RESEARCH AGREEMENT (MRA) is an umbrella framework negotiated once with a repeat corporate partner, under which multiple projects/task orders execute without renegotiating core terms (IP, publication, liability); individual ISRAs/SRAs define scope/budget per project. SRA and MRA merged into one row to stay within the row ceiling. AUDIT 2026-07-18: MIT OSATT page confirms ISRAs and MRAs as authoritative institutional references.
typical_award_size: Highly variable - tens of thousands to several million dollars per project, relationship-dependent (est.)
typical_duration: Project-defined (commonly 1-3 years); a Master Research Agreement sets multi-year umbrella terms
eligibility_window: Any faculty PI whose institution executes a sponsored research agreement with the company
prior_funding_exclusion: no
eligibility_notes: Not a competitive program - access is RELATIONSHIP-DRIVEN. Initiated by faculty-company contact and negotiated through the institution's sponsored research / industry contracts office. Full indirect cost (F&A) rate typically applies; sponsor receives defined deliverables and negotiated IP rights.
review_criteria_official: No formal competitive review; sponsor internal decision plus institutional contract/IP/compliance review.
notes: Distinguished from gifts by: defined scope of work, deliverables/reporting, IP provisions, and full F&A. Typical ranges are estimates; actual amounts vary widely.

program_name: Microsoft Research Fellowship (formerly Microsoft Research PhD Fellowship)
stated_purpose: Create opportunities for faculty, PhD students, and postdocs to collaborate with Microsoft Research on open research challenges that advance science and benefit society.
design_notes: DRIFT CONFIRMED (AUDIT 2026-07-18): funder page verifies this unified 'Microsoft Research Fellowship' (2026 cycle) has replaced the legacy multi-year 'Microsoft Research PhD Fellowship' (and Ada Lovelace Fellowship). It is a challenge-based, direct-application, ONE-TIME collaboration award ($47k US/Canada, $27k Europe, $17k other), distributed as an unrestricted gift to the institution in March/April 2026, spanning PhD students, postdocs, and faculty. Labeled a fellowship per branding though it functions as a research-collaboration award. Original row was accurate.
typical_award_size: Canada/US: $47,000 (one-time); Europe: $27,000; other regions: $17,000. Distributed as a one-time unrestricted gift to the institution (~March/April). Confirmed on funder page.
eligibility_window: Employed or enrolled at a degree-granting university in an eligible region (incl. US); specific challenges accept PhD students, postdocs, faculty, or a combination
specific_topic: Open research challenges across Microsoft Research areas (AI, computer vision, human language technologies, quantum, systems)
prior_funding_exclusion: unspecified
eligibility_notes: Direct (self-submitted) application; faculty proposals may name a student collaborator. Eligibility varies by challenge. Eligible regions include US, Canada, Europe, India, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, Africa, Australia/NZ. Confirmed on funder page.
review_criteria_official: Fit and quality of the proposal against the specific open research challenge; potential to advance science and benefit society.
notes: Challenges span Microsoft Research areas: AI, computer vision, human language technologies, quantum computing, systems, and others.

stated_purpose: Support exceptional PhD students conducting research relevant to GPU computing and its influence on future GPU design, performance, or use.
design_notes: Applicants apply directly (not via institutional nomination) — confirmed on funder page. Fellowship year is the 9-month academic year; the mandatory summer internship precedes it. AUDIT 2026-07-18: 'Submissions now CLOSED' on the page reflects a between-cycle window, not discontinuation; standing annual program.
typical_award_size: Up to $60,000 per award (stipend, tuition, and mandatory fees). Confirmed on funder page.
typical_duration: One academic year (9 months), preceded by a required paid summer internship
eligibility_window: Must have completed at least the first year of PhD study at time of application; enrolled full-time during the fellowship year (funder page references 2026-2027 academic year, graduation no sooner than May/June 2027)
specific_topic: GPU-relevant computing: AI, robotics, autonomous vehicles, graphics, high-performance computing
prior_funding_exclusion: unspecified
eligibility_notes: Direct student application with professor nomination/recommendation letters. International students eligible; internship locations limited to US, Canada, Germany, Sweden, Finland, Switzerland, Israel, and Taiwan (confirmed on funder page).
review_criteria_official: Quality and impact of the research proposal and its potential to influence the design, performance, or use of future GPUs; academic record; recommendation letters.
notes: Focus areas: AI, robotics, autonomous vehicles, graphics, HPC and related GPU-relevant fields.

funder: Pharmaceutical industry (Pfizer, Genentech/Roche, AstraZeneca, Gilead, Merck, et al.)
stated_purpose: Provide financial and/or study-drug support for independent studies where the external investigator serves as the study sponsor, within the company's therapeutic areas of interest.
design_notes: FAMILY row spanning multiple companies' ISR/IIS programs (Pfizer ISR; Genentech/Roche IIS; AstraZeneca ESR; Gilead investigator-sponsored; Merck Investigator Studies Program). In ISS/IIS the EXTERNAL investigator (not the company) is the regulatory Sponsor - distinct from company-sponsored clinical trials. Sourced from Pfizer as representative; per-company terms, portals, and therapeutic areas differ, hence confidence medium. AUDIT 2026-07-18: Pfizer ISR confirmed active (global program, six therapeutic areas incl. internal medicine, batched review windows).
typical_award_size: Varies by company and study; funding and/or study drug/compound support; amounts not publicly fixed
eligibility_window: Qualified investigators (typically physicians/researchers at an institution able to assume the study-sponsor role)
specific_topic: Company-specific therapeutic areas; Pfizer's current six ISR areas (representative): oncology, rare disease, vaccines & antivirals, inflammation & immunology, internal medicine, anti-infectives
prior_funding_exclusion: unspecified
eligibility_notes: Open broadly to researchers who will serve as the study Sponsor (assuming regulatory/sponsor obligations). Company approves scientific merit and alignment with its areas of interest; submitted via each company's grant portal. Application windows are batched and vary by company (confirmed for Pfizer: unsolicited requests accepted only within defined review cycles).
review_criteria_official: Scientific merit, feasibility, and alignment with the company's stated areas of interest; compliance/scientific-independence requirements apply.
notes: Support may be cash, study drug/compound, or both. Therapeutic areas and submission windows vary by company.

stated_purpose: Recognize and fund innovative PhD student research; foster Qualcomm's values of innovation, execution, and teamwork.
design_notes: Award ($50k/entrant) is paid to the university department to fund the students' research expenses; two-person team structure. Limited to participating universities. Separate QIF tracks exist for other regions internationally. AUDIT 2026-07-18: funder page confirms the 2026 North America cohort with '16 winning teams' (matches selectivity).
typical_award_size: $50,000 per entrant (i.e., $100,000 per two-person team), paid to the university department; plus Qualcomm mentorship
eligibility_window: PhD students enrolled for the entire program academic year; two-person teams; at least one member from EE/CS or a related department
prior_funding_exclusion: unspecified
eligibility_notes: Two-person teams; at least one member from Electrical Engineering/Computer Science or related department; enrolled in a PhD program for the full program year. Limited to participating (invited) universities.
selectivity: 16 winning teams selected in the 2026 North America cohort (confirmed on funder page)
review_criteria_official: Innovativeness of the proposal (the fellowship rewards the most innovative proposals); execution and teamwork.
notes: Participating universities include CMU, MIT, Princeton, Stanford, UC Berkeley, UCLA, UCSD, Columbia, Michigan, ASU, and others.

stated_purpose: Fellowships supporting internationally mobile postdocs to carry out research in a new country, with international mobility as a defining criterion.
design_notes: Formerly EMBO Long-Term Fellowships. Applications accepted year-round with periodic deadlines (cadence=rolling; next cutoff 22 Jan 2027). Geographic incoming/outgoing structure relative to EMBC member states is EMBO's established framework; core eligibility facts verified current (2026-07-18).
typical_award_size: Salary or stipend (varies by host country) + relocation allowance + support for fellows with children
eligibility_window: PhD obtained within 2 years before the application submission date
prior_funding_exclusion: no explicit award exclusion; bounded by <=2 yrs since PhD. Confirmed policy change: from the Autumn 2027 round only one EMBO Fellowship application is permitted per applicant, and (from Autumn 2026) a host lab may support only one candidate per round.
eligibility_notes: All nationalities. INTERNATIONAL MOBILITY is a hard requirement: the application must involve movement between countries; applicants may not go to the country where the PhD was obtained, return to a lab where they worked >6 months, or work with their original PhD supervisor. A first-author refereed preprint counts as a first-author publication. Mobility, up-to-2-yr duration, rolling-with-deadline cadence, and the one-application rule confirmed on current EMBO page (2026-07-18).
review_criteria_official: EMBO review: scientific quality and originality of the project, the applicant's track record and potential, and the training/mobility value of the proposed move.
notes: US relevance chiefly for outgoing Europe-to-US and incoming US-to-Europe moves.

stated_purpose: Recognition-and-support programme for outstanding early-career life-science group leaders, providing networking, mentoring, and training within the EMBO Young Investigator network.
design_notes: Included per task specifically to flag the geographic eligibility constraint. Not a research grant - it is a career-development/network membership with modest networking funds. citizenship_residency=host_country_institution_required captures the lab-location gate; institution_type_restriction=other reflects the EMBC/Global-Partner-country requirement. Group-leader window (1-4 yr) and last-author-pub requirement verified current (2026-07-18); an earlier unverifiable '24-28 per round' selectivity figure was removed.
typical_award_size: Financial support for networking over 4 years plus mentoring, training, and access to EMBO/EMBL resources and core facilities; exact amount unspecified
eligibility_window: Independent research group leader for at least 1 and no more than 4 years at the pre-application deadline; no age or years-since-PhD limit
prior_funding_exclusion: unspecified
eligibility_notes: GEOGRAPHIC GATE (key filter, confirmed on current eligibility page): the applicant's independent lab must be located in an EMBC Member State, EMBC Associate Member State, or an EMBO Global Partner (e.g., India, Singapore, Taiwan, Chile). U.S.-based group leaders are GENERALLY NOT ELIGIBLE because the USA is not an EMBC member/associate state or Global Partner; a U.S. researcher qualifies only if they run a lab in an eligible country. Requires >=1 last-author peer-reviewed publication (or verified peer-reviewed preprint) from the independent group.
selectivity: Highly competitive; small annual cohort (exact rate unspecified)
review_criteria_official: EMBO selection: excellence of the research track record and scientific achievements as an independent group leader.
notes: Primary reason for inclusion is to document that U.S.-based PIs are generally excluded.

funder: Fulbright Program (U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs)
stated_purpose: Support U.S. scholars to teach, conduct research, or carry out professional projects abroad to promote international understanding and cooperation.
design_notes: Umbrella program with 380+ awards; concrete eligibility (career stage, degree recency, teaching vs research) is set per individual country/award. Row captures the durable standing program, not a single country award. Verified current on fulbrightscholars.org (2026-07-18).
typical_award_size: Varies by country/award (monthly living stipend + travel and benefits); no single fixed amount published
typical_duration: Several months to a full academic year
eligibility_window: Varies by award type (Early Career: <=7 yrs experience; Mid-Career: >7 and <13 yrs; Senior: >13 yrs; Distinguished: >7 yrs; Postdoctoral: doctorate conferred within 5-7 years before award start)
prior_funding_exclusion: yes: recipients must wait two years after completing a prior Fulbright award before reapplying
eligibility_notes: U.S. citizenship required by the application deadline; permanent residency is NOT sufficient (confirmed on current page). Ineligible if resided abroad 5+ of the preceding 6 years (9+ months in a calendar year counts as a full year). Grantee goes abroad to teach, research, or pursue a professional project in one of 120+ countries. Career-stage and degree-recency requirements vary by the specific country/award (Early Career, Mid-Career, Senior, Distinguished, Postdoctoral).
selectivity: 380+ awards across 120+ countries (confirmed on funder page); per-award rate unspecified
review_criteria_official: Discipline peer-review panels plus binational commission/post review: quality and feasibility of the project, applicant qualifications, and contribution to the Fulbright objective of mutual understanding.
notes: Administered by IIE/CIES for State Dept ECA. Award variants by country and by type (Teaching, Research, Teaching/Research, Distinguished Scholar, Postdoctoral).

funder: Fulbright Program (U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs)
stated_purpose: Grants for U.S. graduating seniors, graduate students, and young professionals to study, conduct research, or teach English abroad.
design_notes: Grant types are variants of one program: Study/Research Awards (incl. creative/performing arts), English Teaching Assistant (ETA), Fulbright-National Geographic, and Fulbright-Fogarty (public health).
